messages:
anya: heads up — during last night's canary we saw a reconnect storm from the web client and the billing dashboard shows duplicated token charges. dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/streams/canary-2026 :eyes:
praveen: ugh. any repro steps or logs?
anya: qps spike ~02:12 UTC, a bunch of clients restarted and started resume requests. logs show repeated `resume_id` reuse across different sockets.
maria: do you mean clients reusing the same resume token across tabs? that can cause duplicate prefix replay.
anya: yep. but the weird bit: server telemetry shows two resume-accepted events per resume_id in same second, then two billing events.
sam: canary had the sticky-region routing enabled. maybe session affinity caused route swap + proxy pool reuse?
praveen: sticky routing should still dedupe resume tokens. are we missing namespace isolation between shards?
anya: attaching excerpt from proxy logs: ```
[02:12:11] proxy-12 recv RESUME id=abc123 client=web-9
[02:12:11] proxy-12 forward RESUME id=abc123 -> runtime-a
[02:12:11] runtime-a accept RESUME id=abc123 alloc=session-7
[02:12:11] proxy-8 recv RESUME id=abc123 client=web-9
[02:12:11] proxy-8 forward RESUME id=abc123 -> runtime-b
[02:12:11] runtime-b accept RESUME id=abc123 alloc=session-7
```
praveen: interesting — two proxies forwarded same resume to different runtimes because the routing table briefly had duplicate owner entries during rollout.
maria: that suggests a window where lease handoff isn't atomic. we probably need a single-writer semantics or a short tombstone to prevent second accept.
sam: could be compounded by the client polyfill. some older browsers open two EventSource connections for redundancy and both try to resume. did we see duplicate client IDs?
anya: client id was identical in logs, yes. but the resume_id collision still shouldn't create double billing. why are billing events emitted per accept?
praveen: because our charge path currently counts accepted session allocations, not deduped resume tokens. accept -> allocate -> charge. if two runtimes accept, two charges.
devexp-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-21T01:58 promoted to 30% (sha: a1b2c3).
anya: timeline aligns with that canary.
maria: action item: make resume accept idempotent at the allocation layer. i.e., allocation should check a global resume lease table and refuse second accept OR return existing allocation without charging.
sam: can we patch billing to accept idempotent acknowledges? adding dedupe in billing will avoid immediate double-charges while we fix routing.
praveen: short-term mitigation: revert sticky-region flag for canary or reduce canary traffic to 0% to stop rollouts from touching route tables. longer-term: add lease compare-and-swap in the handoff.
anya: also saw a bump in console metric `stream.resume.latency` during the window — maybe due to extra network hops.
maria: telemetry note: console's current sampling masks duplicate-accepts because we sample by request id, not resume_id. we should add resume_id as a dimension.
anya: +1. otherwise it looks like normal, hiding the real duplication. made debugging harder.
sam: quick repro idea: simulate dual-proxy forwarding with a tiny race script and see if two runtimes accept. i can hack something this morning.
praveen: also check proxy keepalive behavior — one proxy returned `204` before forwarding and the client retried -> second proxy picked it up. proxy half-close might trigger duplicate forward.
maria: please paste the chunked SSE envelope we saw. that polyfill seems to send an extra `:heartbeat` comment which we interpreted as an event boundary.
anya: snippet: ```
data: {"type":"patch","cursor":"abc"}
\n:heartbeat
\n```
praveen: we treat comment lines as no-op, but some proxies reframe them into separate frames and the client polyfill triggers a reconnect on certain comment sequences. weird.
sam: client polyfill maintainers said they added aggressive reconnect for stale comments (they thought browsers drop commented keepalives).
anya: result: two sockets open, both resume, both accepted, double charge.
praveen: mitigation checklist:
- revert sticky-region on current canary (sam)
- add resume_id dimension to resume telemetry (maria)
- billing dedupe patch to safely ignore duplicate allocation for same resume_id within 30s window (praveen)
- investigate lease CAS to prevent double accept (infra plan)
- follow up with client teams about polyfill behavior and recommend backoff (devexp)
maria: i can push telemetry change right after standup. also will add dashboard alert when resume_accepts/second_accepts ratio > 0.01.
sam: rolled back sticky routing on canary, monitoring now.
anya: can confirm metric spike stopped after rollback. console shows no new duplicate accept events for 10m.
praveen: created issue #INF-1842 for allocation idempotency and billing dedupe RFC.
devexp-bot: ping @devexp for client polyfill contact.
anya: @maria @praveen please keep me in the loop. thanks team :heart:
praveen: gonna draft a tiny patch to billing to check `resume_id` in charge path — low risk hotfix.
anya: sounds good. I'll open a postmortem doc and link to it here when ready.
release-bot: note: rollback of feature/sticky-region to canary at 1733334462 completed by sam.
anya: closing loop — no user-facing billing impacts detected yet but we should treat this as near-miss and tighten resume semantics.
